```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = '#>', eval = FALSE)
```

A generated wrapper returns when the service has answered. Until then the R
session does nothing else, so a Shiny app that calls a slow wrapper stops
responding to every user. This guide is for the person calling a wrapper from
such an app. It needs no change to the client: the call runs in a second R
process, a worker, and the session gets a promise for the result. The examples
use a hypothetical client package `myclient` with a wrapper `get_items()`, and
[mirai](https://mirai.r-lib.org) for the workers.

## The recipe

Start the workers once, when the app starts:

```{r daemons}
mirai::daemons(2)
```

Wrap the call in `mirai::mirai()` and pass its inputs by name. It returns at
once, and promises treats the returned object as a promise:

```{r promise}
task <- mirai::mirai(myclient::get_items(category = category), category = 'books')
promises::then(task, function(items) message(length(items), ' items'))
```

In Shiny, give the same call to an `ExtendedTask`. The task reports whether it
is running, and the app stays responsive in the meantime:

```{r extended-task}
server <- function(input, output, session) {
  items <- shiny::ExtendedTask$new(function(category) {
    mirai::mirai(myclient::get_items(category = category), category = category)
  })
  shiny::observeEvent(input$search, items$invoke(input$category))
  output$status <- shiny::renderText(items$status())
  output$table <- shiny::renderTable(items$result())
}
```

A wrapper that fetches every page or sends a batch runs whole inside the
worker; the promise resolves once, with the combined result.

## What a worker needs

A worker is a new R process. It shares nothing with the session except what it
is sent and what it finds on the machine.

- **The client package, installed.** Call the wrapper as `myclient::get_items()`
  so the worker loads the package from its library. A package loaded with
  `pkgload::load_all()` exists only in the session.
- **Credentials.** A worker started on the same machine inherits the environment
  variables that exist when `mirai::daemons()` runs. Set credentials in the
  deployment environment or `.Renviron`, before the workers start. A variable set
  later with `Sys.setenv()` reaches only the session.
- **Options.** `options()` set in the session, such as
  `options(myclient.request = ...)` or `options(myclient.dry_run = TRUE)`, do
  not reach a worker. Set them there as well:

```{r everywhere}
mirai::everywhere(
  options(myclient.request = request),
  request = getOption('myclient.request')
)
```

## The response cache

A client with a [response cache](configuration.html#response-cache)
keeps a `disk` store in the user's cache directory, so the session and every
worker read and write the same entries, provided they run as the same user and
resolve the same cache directory (`tools::R_user_dir()`). A `memory` store belongs to one process: each
worker has its own, and the session does not see what a worker stored.

An entry is shared only when the key matches. The key includes a hash of the
credential and the package's request and response-policy options, so a worker that lacks an
option the session has set stores its results under a different key.

## Errors

When the wrapper fails in the worker, the promise is rejected with an error
that carries the wrapper's message. The class of the original condition does
not cross the process boundary, so a handler has to match on the message.
`promises::then(task, onRejected = ...)` receives the error, and an
`ExtendedTask` raises it again from `task$result()`, which Shiny shows as an
output error.

## Limits

- A worker runs one call at a time. Further calls wait for a free worker, so
  start as many workers as the app needs calls in flight.
- The result is copied back to the session. A large result costs that copy in
  time and memory.
- Do not return or log a dry-run request from a worker. It can hold
  credentials.
- Only mirai is tested with generated clients. Any pool whose task becomes a
  promise fits the same recipe, for example `promises::future_promise()` with
  the future package. mizu has not been tried here.

The alternative to workers is a request helper that performs the request
asynchronously inside the session, with `httr2::req_perform_promise()`. It
needs no second process, but paging, batching and retries would each need a
promise-aware version, so generated clients do not offer it.
